passage: Right at the centre of the living room, Tejas squeezed both eyes shut, pressed both hands over them and stood very still. Jasleen, Tejas's older cousin, finished counting and turned round. "Found you!" Jasleen laughed. Tejas uncovered and looked stunned. "But I could not see you!" The round was over almost before it began, and Tejas's lip trembled.

qa.q: Where did Tejas stand while covering both eyes?
qa.a: Tejas stood at the centre of the living room.

qa.q: What was Tejas feeling when Jasleen said "Found you!"?
qa.a: Tejas was stunned and upset, because Tejas believed that not seeing meant not being seen, which is why the lip trembled.

qa.q: What alternative could Tejas try next round, and why?
qa.a: Tejas could run behind the sofa or a curtain while Jasleen counts, because hiding needs a place where the seeker cannot see.

qa.q: How does Jasleen see Tejas standing with hands over the eyes?
qa.a: Jasleen sees the child in plain view and laughs at the easy find, likely not realising how upset Tejas will be.

grounding: A four-year-old covers both eyes in the middle of the room and believes nobody can see, unable to take the seeker's point of view.

passage:
"Ready or not!" Sangeeta shouted from the stairs.
Right at the centre of the living room, Ujjwal, who was four, clapped both hands over his eyes.
"Where's Ujjwal?" Sangeeta called, walking right up to him.
"You can't see me!"
"Um... I can see you."
"No! My eyes are closed!"
Sangeeta giggled and poked his tummy. "Found you."
"No fair!"

qa.a: Right at the centre of the living room.

qa.q: What was Ujjwal thinking when he said "You can't see me!"?
qa.a: He was sure and happy that covering his eyes hid him, and felt it was unfair when he was found.

qa.q: What could Sangeeta do to help Ujjwal hide better?
qa.a: She could show him a spot behind the curtain and explain that she sees him even when his eyes are closed.

qa.q: How does the game look to Sangeeta?
qa.a: Sangeeta finds it funny and sweet, giggling because he is in plain view.

grounding: A four-year-old covers his eyes in the middle of the room and believes nobody can see him, not yet taking the seeker's view.

passage:
Kindergarten note for Gurpreet's parents, from Sabina
At hide-and-seek, Gurpreet, four, stood at the centre of the carpet with both hands over her eyes and whispered, "I'm hiding." The seeker walked straight to her. She was surprised to be found. Later I stood behind the door and asked, "Can you see me?" She thought, then went to hide behind the shelf.

qa.q: Where did Gurpreet stand to hide?
qa.a: At the centre of the carpet.

qa.q: What was Gurpreet feeling when the seeker found her?
qa.a: She was surprised and maybe a bit confused, since she believed covering her eyes kept her hidden.

qa.q: What worked well in Sabina's response?
qa.a: Letting Gurpreet feel what it's like to look for someone helped her see the seeker's view and move behind the shelf.

qa.q: What would change for the seeker if Gurpreet hid behind the shelf?
qa.a: The seeker would actually have to search, which makes the game more fun for them.

grounding: A teacher's note describes a four-year-old who covers her eyes on the carpet and thinks she is hidden, then learns to hide behind something.
